newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy mkt sees o/n rate falling sharply.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy mkt sees o/n rate falling sharply.

text.p: The Italian money market sees the overnight rate below the 8.25-percent discount rate a month, indicating that it expects a rate cut in the near future, a study by Bocconi University's research arm Igier showed.

On a one-month horizon, the implicit overnight rate was seen at 8.18 percent, down from an official market close of 8.31 percent on Thursday, the day on which Igier based its study. Early on Friday, the actual overnight rate was 8.25 percent.
On a three month horizon, the implicit overnight rate was expected at 7.97 percent, lower than last week's forecast of 8.21 percent.
A week ago, the implicit overnight rate was expected to b e 8.31 percent on a one-month horizon. A month ago, the rate was forecast at 8.51 percent in the same time horizon.
The Bank of Italy last cut its official discount rate to 8.25 percent from 9.00 percent on July 24 and lowered its fixed-term advances, or Lombard, rate to 9.75 percent from 10.50 percent.
Financial markets have speculated in the past two days about the possibility of a near-term easing, following the government's tougher-than-expected budget package for 1997.
But the Bank of Italy said earlier monetary policy remained aimed at pushing average inflation below 3.0 percent in 1997.
On a one year horizon, the implicit overnight rate was seen at 7.64 percent, lower than last week's 8.04 percent forecast.
In two year's time, the implicit overnight rate was expected to drop to 7.93 percent, compared with 8.27 percent a week ago.

The spread between this rate and the implicit German overnight rate, considered to be a good indicator of market confidence in Economic and Monetary Union, fell to 293 basis points from 312 basis points a week ago and 336 one month ago.
